A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A-I are readable and support a complete comparison despite layout changes.

before.justification: v5 reports original numerical simulations, MPI3D-Complex and Causal3DIdent experiments, and an OpenCLIP case study in Section 5 and Appendices D-G.

after.justification: v7 retains these original empirical results, including semantic recovery, downstream prediction, OOD evaluation and zero-shot concept classification.

M1.justification: The latent-variable model, selection and perturbation mechanisms, MMCL objectives and encoding procedures remain unchanged. Replacing the generic similarity notation with κ in Equation (1) does not change the objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same simulations, MPI3D-Complex, Causal3DIdent and LAION-400M/OpenCLIP case study with 146 concepts and Flickr images. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same comparison methods, including linear and nonlinear probes and the OpenCLIP ViT-B-32 and ViT-L-14 variants. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Data splits, bias settings, encoder dimensions, training budgets and evaluation procedures match. Numerical simulations retain 100,000 training iterations, MPI3D-Complex retains 200,000 steps, and the R2, MCC and macro-F1 metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the encoding-size ablations, combined-bias experiment, linearity analyses, OOD tests and OpenCLIP confusion matrices. Tables 4-5 and Figures 11-23 contain existing analyses redistributed across appendix pages.

E5.justification: Three-seed averaging in Section 5 and Appendices D-F remains unchanged, as do the plotted variability displays. Neither version introduces different run counts or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Main-text and appendix results match, including Tables 4-5 and the figure graphics. For example, Figure 10 retains Animal macro-F1 scores of 97.6% for ViT-B-32 and 98.9% for ViT-L-14.

T1.justification: The assumptions, definitions, identifiability theorem, corollaries and Appendix C proofs are substantively unchanged. The similarity-symbol replacement and wording about variable realizations introduce no new mathematical condition or proof step.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims that MMCL identifies unbiased shared semantics and that misalignment can harm semantic coverage or support invariant representation learning, depending on the task.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving latent dependence, quantization, ambiguous text and caption coverage remain unchanged. Appendix I retains the same limitations and future directions; retitling its bias-estimation paragraph does not change its substance.

D1.justification: The first-page access information changes from a direct GitHub code link to a project-page link. Implementation settings and computation-resource disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish any change in actual code availability.

R1.justification: Both retain the same 83 cited works and research positioning, including Appendix B. Several reference URLs change, but these are bibliographic access updates rather than additions or removals of research.

P1.justification: v7 makes limited wording and notation refinements, standardizes headings and appendix references, updates the corresponding author and conference information, and adds acknowledgments and funding disclosure. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Title formatting, table typography and appendix figure/table placement change. For example, Figure 22 moves from page 40 to 43 and Table 12 from page 41 to 40. The graphics and substantive table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v7 provides modest gains in clarity and transparency through explicit similarity-function notation, more precise wording about realizations in Appendix C, and funding disclosure. The unchanged theory, empirical evidence and limitations keep the overall improvement limited; the revised link alone does not establish improved reproducibility.
